beliefs.practice: Keep a single, long-lived MongoClient instance per process (reuse across requests) and configure an appropriate connection pool (e.g., maxPoolSize) rather than opening/closing clients per request.

Store the DOCUMENTDB_URI and any embedding provider keys (OPENAI_API_KEY) only in environment variables or a secret store (e.g., Azure Key Vault); never check connection strings or keys into source control or write them to logs.
Use TLS by default (require TLS/SSL=true in the connection string) and validate server certificates (do not disable certificate verification).

Design documents with a dedicated typed embedding field (e.g., embedding: [float32]) and include explicit metadata fields used for filtering (name, indications, dosage) so vector search can be combined with metadata filters; keep embedding dimension constant across all documents.

Create a vector index on the embedding field specifying the appropriate index type and parameters for the workload (algorithm: HNSW or DiskANN, metric: cosine or dot_product, dimension: <embedding_dim>, and tune M/efConstruction/efSearch or equivalent) so nearest-neighbor queries use the vector index instead of full collection scans.

Also create conventional indexes on fields used for equality/filtered queries (e.g., name, drug_class, is_active) and on any metadata fields used in combination with vector queries to enable efficient hybrid search filtering.

When seeding/upserting many documents with embeddings, use bulkWrite / bulk upsert operations with ordered=false and reasonable batch sizes to improve throughput and tolerate per-document failures without aborting the whole batch.

Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries of transient errors (network timeouts, 5xx server errors, rate limits), cap max retries, and make write operations idempotent (use upserts or deterministic document IDs) to safely retry.

Limit fields returned from DocumentDB queries (projection) to only what the endpoint needs (e.g., name, indications, score) to minimize network IO and deserialization time when returning top-N results.

For vector similarity ranking, request a small top-k (e.g., 10) from the DB and perform any additional re-ranking or business-logic scoring in the application layer rather than retrieving large candidate sets from the DB.

Store embeddings as float32 (not string) and, if supported by the server, use a native vector field type rather than an array of numbers to take advantage of vector indexes and store size/perf optimizations.

When performing vector + metadata hybrid queries, ensure the metadata filters are covered by indexes or applied as early as possible (index intersection or compound indexes) so the vector index has a smaller candidate set to search.

Use explain()/queryPlanner (or the MCP server tools) after creating indexes and running representative vector and metadata queries to verify the query uses the vector index and to measure candidate counts and execution time.
Protect the DocumentDB endpoint with network controls: restrict allowed client IPs, use VNet/private endpoints or firewalls, and avoid exposing the database publicly without IP restrictions.

Rate-limit and batch calls to the external embedding provider (e.g., OpenAI): cache embeddings for identical inputs, and back off on 429/429-like responses to avoid bursting through provider quotas during seeding or requests.
Use deterministic document IDs (e.g., hash of canonicalized drug name + normalized fields) or unique constraints to prevent accidental duplicate formulary entries and make upserts idempotent.

Avoid inefficient full-collection scans for similarity by verifying that the vector index exists and that queries use the index; as a fallback, fail safely (limit scan size) rather than returning extremely slow responses.

Instrument and record key metrics (query latency, vector index candidate counts, top-k retrieval time, index build time, failed upserts, embedding provider errors) and enable slow query profiling to detect regressions with production data.

When creating collections, set appropriate storage and throughput settings for the expected workload (pre-create collections with the sample_healthcare_10 database, provisioned RU/throughput if applicable) and avoid creating very small collections that will be inefficient to index and serve vectors.

Protect logs and error traces so they do not contain full user clinical intents or embedding vectors (PII/PHI); treat clinical query text as sensitive and redact it from persistent logs unless explicitly allowed and encrypted.
